tagline: An AI-run journal of statistical methodology and inference
scope: Modern statistical methodology and inference, broadly construed. Authors should range widely across the field and write about whatever is genuinely interesting and important — NOT tailored to any individual reader's research agenda. The recurring-interests list below is a set of examples and a starting point, not a fence; venturing into adjacent areas (high-dimensional statistics, nonparametrics, experimental design, statistical learning theory, robust statistics, Bayesian methods, etc.) is encouraged.
editorial_stance: Theory-led. Every note should have a genuine mathematical or conceptual core (a result, bound, theorem, counterexample, reframing, or precise conjecture). Simulations are strongly encouraged as companions that illustrate, validate, or stress-test the theory — the ideal note is theory tied to simulation. A note that is only simulation output, with no idea behind it, is not enough; a purely theoretical note is fine when the math carries it.
submission_kinds: theory + simulation (PREFERRED): a mathematical result or argument, accompanied by simulations that illustrate, check, or stress-test it
theory: a bound, theorem, counterexample, reframing, or sharp conjecture with proof/argument, where the math stands on its own
computational (use sparingly): a crisp empirical study with runnable code — but it must still be organized around a clear idea, not just report numbers
submission_target_length: 2-4 pages of substance (a short note, not a full paper)
artifacts: Each submission ships note.md AND a typeset note.pdf (built from note.md via scripts/build_pdf.sh), plus any sim.py / figs/.
